title: Corporate Law Midterm Examination Part 1
description: Advanced conceptual quiz covering corporate personality, company formation, company types, agency, and incorporation principles under Sri Lankan Corporate Law.
subject: LAW2372 - Corporate Law

questions.question: Which statement best reflects the doctrine of separate legal personality?
options: A company and its shareholders are treated as a single legal person for contractual liability.
A company exists as a legal entity distinct from its members after incorporation.
A company remains legally dependent upon its directors throughout its existence.
A company acquires legal personality only after issuing shares to the public.
questions.answer: A company exists as a legal entity distinct from its members after incorporation.
questions.rationale: Separate legal personality recognizes the company as an independent legal entity.

questions.question: The principal legal significance of Salomon v Salomon is that it established which principle?
options: Directors are always personally liable for company debts.
A company's legal identity depends upon the number of shareholders.
An incorporated company is legally separate from its incorporators.
Creditors may always proceed directly against shareholders.
questions.answer: An incorporated company is legally separate from its incorporators.
questions.rationale: The case confirmed the independent legal personality of companies.

questions.question: Emma wishes to protect her personal assets while operating a café. Which structure is generally the most appropriate?
questions.answer: Private limited company
questions.rationale: A private limited company generally limits members' liability.

questions.question: Two companies combine resources under a formal agreement to complete a single solar project while sharing returns according to contribution. Which arrangement is most accurate?
questions.answer: Joint venture
questions.rationale: The arrangement possesses the defining characteristics of a joint venture.

questions.question: Following incorporation of NextGen Tech Solutions Pvt Ltd, which combination most accurately describes its legal consequences?
options: Separate legal personality, limited liability, and registration under company law.
Unlimited liability, partnership status, and automatic tax exemption.
questions.answer: Separate legal personality, limited liability, and registration under company law.
questions.rationale: These are fundamental consequences of incorporation.

questions.question: A loan is obtained solely in the company's name and the business later fails. Under the doctrine of incorporation, who ordinarily bears liability?
questions.answer: The company itself
questions.rationale: Company debts belong primarily to the incorporated company.

questions.question: A former manager creates a deceptively similar company name to evade obligations and mislead customers. Which judicial response is most appropriate?
options: Lifting the corporate veil where fraud or deception is established
Treating both companies as permanently merged
questions.answer: Lifting the corporate veil where fraud or deception is established
questions.rationale: Courts may disregard separate personality where fraud or abuse exists.

questions.question: Where the articles are silent, which execution method ordinarily satisfies company contract requirements?
options: Two directors or one director together with the secretary
questions.answer: Two directors or one director together with the secretary
questions.rationale: This is the recognized execution method where articles provide no alternative.

questions.question: Which statement best explains shareholder protection in a limited liability company?
options: Shareholders are always liable for unpaid company debts.
Protection generally applies except where fraud or similar misconduct justifies personal liability.
Liability protection applies only while profits are earned.
questions.answer: Protection generally applies except where fraud or similar misconduct justifies personal liability.
questions.rationale: Limited liability is not absolute where fraud exists.

questions.question: Before incorporation, Sara collects deposits using the proposed company. When may she become personally liable?
options: Whenever shareholders disagree with the project
Whenever the company makes a trading loss
Where pre incorporation dealings involve fraud or similar misconduct
questions.answer: Where pre incorporation dealings involve fraud or similar misconduct
questions.rationale: Pre incorporation contracts and fraudulent conduct may create personal liability.

questions.question: Why is the proposed company name Sri Lanka National Tours likely to be rejected?
options: It exceeds the permitted number of words.
It misleadingly suggests a governmental connection.
questions.answer: It misleadingly suggests a governmental connection.
questions.rationale: Certain names implying state affiliation are restricted.

questions.question: One founder dies several years after incorporation. Which principle ensures the company's continued existence?
questions.answer: Perpetual succession
questions.rationale: The company's existence continues independently of its members.

questions.question: Converting from a private company to a public company generally results in which consequence?
options: Greater disclosure obligations and broader shareholder participation
questions.answer: Greater disclosure obligations and broader shareholder participation
questions.rationale: Public companies operate under stricter governance standards.

questions.question: What is the defining legal feature of a subsidiary relationship?
options: Complete operational independence from every parent entity
Control exercised by a parent company over governance or operations
Mandatory equal ownership by all shareholders
questions.answer: Control exercised by a parent company over governance or operations
questions.rationale: A subsidiary is characterized by parent company control.

questions.question: A company limited by guarantee converts into a public company. Which outcome most accurately follows?
options: Dividend distribution becomes possible subject to applicable rules.
questions.answer: Dividend distribution becomes possible subject to applicable rules.
questions.rationale: Conversion changes the company's operational and financial model.

questions.question: A non profit organization wishes to avoid issuing shares while limiting member liability. Which company form is appropriate?
questions.answer: Company limited by guarantee
questions.rationale: Guarantee companies suit non profit objectives.

questions.question: Which combination best reflects principal risks associated with offshore companies?
options: Lower administration and complete immunity from regulation
Tax avoidance allegations together with regulatory and reputational risks
Automatic domestic tax exemption and unlimited secrecy
questions.answer: Tax avoidance allegations together with regulatory and reputational risks
questions.rationale: Offshore structures create significant compliance and reputation risks.

questions.question: A foreign incorporated company establishes a place of business in Sri Lanka. How must it generally register?
questions.answer: As an overseas company
questions.rationale: Foreign incorporated companies register as overseas companies.

questions.question: An authorized agent concludes a contract on behalf of the principal. Who is ordinarily bound?
questions.answer: The principal
questions.rationale: Authorized agency binds the principal.

questions.question: A ship captain sells perishable cargo during an emergency after being unable to contact the owner. Which legal principles best justify the sale?
options: Agency by ratification and constructive notice
Agency of necessity together with the doctrine of salvage
questions.answer: Agency of necessity together with the doctrine of salvage
questions.rationale: Emergency necessity may justify otherwise unauthorized action.

questions.question: Joe routinely enters contracts on behalf of X Ltd with Harry's knowledge despite lacking express authority. Which type of agency is most accurately created toward third parties acting in good faith?
options: Agency by estoppel or implied authority
questions.answer: Agency by estoppel or implied authority
questions.rationale: Consistent conduct accepted by the company creates implied or apparent authority.

questions.question: Apparent authority arises primarily when:
options: The principal's conduct reasonably represents that the agent possesses authority.
The agent privately believes they possess authority.
The board later approves every transaction.
The third party independently assumes authority without representation.
questions.answer: The principal's conduct reasonably represents that the agent possesses authority.
questions.rationale: Apparent authority depends upon representations attributable to the principal.

questions.question: In a standard agency transaction, who are generally regarded as the contracting parties?
options: The principal and the third party
The company secretary and the third party
questions.answer: The principal and the third party
questions.rationale: The agent acts as an intermediary while the contract binds principal and third party.

questions.question: Following an unauthorized transaction, may a principal ratify only the beneficial parts while rejecting the remainder?
options: No, ratification must apply to the entire transaction.
Yes, whenever the agent exceeded authority.
questions.answer: No, ratification must apply to the entire transaction.
questions.rationale: Partial ratification is generally ineffective.

questions.question: Which combination of circumstances is essential before agency of necessity can arise?
options: Urgency, impossibility of contacting the principal, and good faith action
Written authorization together with shareholder approval
Financial benefit to both principal and agent
questions.answer: Urgency, impossibility of contacting the principal, and good faith action
questions.rationale: Agency of necessity requires an emergency, inability to obtain instructions, and good faith.

questions.question: A general manager signs a renovation contract outside actual authority, but the contractor reasonably believes authority exists based on prior dealings. Which principle most likely binds the company?
questions.answer: Apparent authority
questions.rationale: Previous conduct may create apparent authority upon which third parties rely.

questions.question: A principal remains silent for several months after learning of an unauthorized sale. Under which circumstance is silence most likely treated as ratification?
options: Where silence reasonably indicates acceptance and the third party relies upon it
Whenever the transaction produced a profit
questions.answer: Where silence reasonably indicates acceptance and the third party relies upon it
questions.rationale: Silence combined with reliance may amount to implied ratification or estoppel.

questions.question: A marketing manager breaches an internal restriction unknown to a long standing supplier. Under what principle might the supplier enforce the agreement?
options: Indoor management supported by apparent authority
questions.answer: Indoor management supported by apparent authority
questions.rationale: Third parties acting in good faith may rely upon apparent authority and indoor management.

questions.question: An agent exceeds purchasing authority and secretly profits from the transaction. Which fiduciary obligation has primarily been breached?
options: Duty to preserve confidential information only
Duty to avoid conflicts of interest and secret profits
Duty to maximize the agent's commission
Duty to negotiate the highest available price
questions.answer: Duty to avoid conflicts of interest and secret profits
questions.rationale: Agents must avoid conflicts and account for unauthorized profits.

questions.question: A CEO publicly introduces an independent contractor as the company's operations agent. Which doctrine may prevent the company from denying authority later?
questions.answer: Agency by estoppel
questions.rationale: Representations by the principal may estop denial of authority.

questions.question: An undisclosed principal generally cannot intervene in a contract where:
options: Intervention would materially alter the contractual rights originally agreed.
questions.answer: Intervention would materially alter the contractual rights originally agreed.
questions.rationale: Undisclosed principals cannot intervene where doing so fundamentally changes the bargain.

questions.question: According to Cooke and Sons v Eshelby, which statement is most accurate regarding an undisclosed principal?
options: The undisclosed principal can sue the buyer, subject to applicable limitations.
The undisclosed principal never acquires contractual rights.
Only the agent may recover payment.
questions.answer: The undisclosed principal can sue the buyer, subject to applicable limitations.
questions.rationale: The case recognizes the rights of an undisclosed principal.

questions.question: An agent reroutes a vessel to protect cargo during severe weather, increasing costs. When is indemnity most likely available?
options: Where the decision was reasonable and necessary to protect the principal's interests.
Whenever the principal later benefits financially.
questions.answer: Where the decision was reasonable and necessary to protect the principal's interests.
questions.rationale: Necessary and reasonable protective actions generally justify indemnity.

questions.question: Which event may automatically terminate an agency relationship by operation of law?
questions.answer: Mental incapacity of the agent
questions.rationale: Mental incapacity can terminate an agency relationship.

questions.question: Which agency relationship is capable of taking effect retrospectively?
questions.answer: Agency by ratification
questions.rationale: Ratification validates a previously unauthorized act retrospectively.

questions.question: An undisclosed agency exists where:
options: The agent contracts without revealing the identity or existence of the principal.
The principal signs every contract personally.
questions.answer: The agent contracts without revealing the identity or existence of the principal.
questions.rationale: The third party is unaware that the agent acts for another.

questions.question: Which combination best represents the core fiduciary duties of an agent?
options: Obedience, diligence, accounting, good faith, disclosure, and avoidance of conflicts
Profit maximization, delegation, secrecy, and investment discretion
Personal enrichment, confidentiality, and independent contracting
questions.answer: Obedience, diligence, accounting, good faith, disclosure, and avoidance of conflicts
questions.rationale: These are the principal fiduciary obligations owed by an agent.

questions.question: A bank relies upon a company's apparent compliance with its Articles of Association despite undisclosed internal irregularities. Which principle primarily protects the bank?
questions.answer: Indoor Management Rule
questions.rationale: The indoor management rule protects outsiders dealing in good faith.

questions.question: Mahony v East Holyford Mining Co. primarily supports which proposition?
options: Outsiders may assume internal procedures have been properly complied with.
Every outsider is deemed to know internal resolutions.
questions.answer: Outsiders may assume internal procedures have been properly complied with.
questions.rationale: The case reinforces the indoor management rule.

questions.question: A proposed amendment to a company's articles increases an existing member's liability. Which statement is legally correct?
options: The member's liability cannot generally be increased without consent.
The amendment binds every member immediately.
A simple board resolution is sufficient.
Directors may impose additional liability unilaterally.
questions.answer: The member's liability cannot generally be increased without consent.
questions.rationale: Members are protected against compulsory increases in liability.

questions.question: Which situation most accurately represents an application of the doctrine of ultra vires under company law?
options: A company enters into a transaction expressly prohibited by its objects or constitutional limitations.
A director exceeds an internally delegated spending limit without the outsider's knowledge.
A shareholder votes against a special resolution at a general meeting.
A company fails to file its annual return within the prescribed period.
questions.answer: A company enters into a transaction expressly prohibited by its objects or constitutional limitations.
questions.rationale: Ultra vires concerns acts beyond the company's constitutional authority.

questions.question: A company's articles require board approval before making outside investments. An outsider contracts without knowledge of this internal restriction. Which doctrine most strongly protects the outsider?
questions.answer: Indoor Management Rule
questions.rationale: The Indoor Management Rule protects outsiders acting in good faith from undisclosed internal irregularities.

questions.question: A mortgage bond requiring signatures of three directors is executed by only two. According to The Jupiter Cigarette and Tobacco Co. Ltd. v H.C. Henry Soysa, what is the most appropriate legal outcome?
options: The company may still be bound where the lender relied in good faith upon apparent compliance with internal procedures.
The transaction is automatically void because every constitutional requirement was not fulfilled.
The directors become personally liable while the company is fully discharged.
The mortgage remains suspended until shareholder ratification is obtained.
questions.answer: The company may still be bound where the lender relied in good faith upon apparent compliance with internal procedures.
questions.rationale: The case illustrates protection afforded to outsiders relying upon apparent regularity.

questions.question: Galaxy Holdings Ltd borrows funds for an activity allegedly outside its stated objects. Following Peoples Bank v Yashodha Holdings, which conclusion is most consistent with modern company law?
options: The company cannot simply avoid liability by alleging the transaction was ultra vires.
Every agreement beyond the object clause is automatically void against all parties.
The lender loses all contractual rights regardless of good faith.
The directors alone become borrowers under the agreement.
questions.answer: The company cannot simply avoid liability by alleging the transaction was ultra vires.
questions.rationale: Modern company law significantly limits reliance on ultra vires to escape contractual obligations.

questions.question: Which category of company is specifically required to include an object clause within its Articles of Association?
questions.answer: Company limited by guarantee
questions.rationale: Guarantee companies ordinarily require an object clause defining their purposes.

questions.question: The primary legal purpose of a company's prospectus is to:
options: Provide prospective investors with material information necessary to make informed investment decisions.
Appoint the first directors of the company.
Replace the Articles of Association after incorporation.
Serve as the company's annual financial report.
questions.answer: Provide prospective investors with material information necessary to make informed investment decisions.
questions.rationale: A prospectus ensures adequate disclosure to potential investors.

questions.question: Formal decisions passed collectively by shareholders are known as:
questions.answer: Resolutions
questions.rationale: Shareholders exercise decision-making power through resolutions.

questions.question: What level of shareholder approval is generally required for a special resolution?
options: More than 75 percent of votes cast
More than 50 percent of votes cast
Exactly two thirds of all shareholders
questions.answer: More than 75 percent of votes cast
questions.rationale: Special resolutions generally require a 75 percent majority.

questions.question: Following the introduction of the Companies Act No. 07 of 2007, which document ceased to be a constitutional document of a company?
questions.answer: Memorandum of Association
questions.rationale: The Memorandum no longer functions as a constitutional document under the 2007 Act.

questions.question: Which type of company may register under Sri Lankan law but is prohibited from carrying on business within Sri Lanka?
questions.answer: Offshore company
questions.rationale: Offshore companies are subject to restrictions on conducting business within Sri Lanka.

questions.question: What liability may arise where a prospectus contains untrue statements?
options: Both civil liability and criminal liability may arise against responsible persons.
No liability arises if the company was incorporated.
questions.answer: Both civil liability and criminal liability may arise against responsible persons.
questions.rationale: The Companies Act provides both civil and criminal consequences for misleading prospectuses.

questions.question: Which meetings must generally be open to invitation for all shareholders entitled to participate?
questions.answer: General meetings
questions.rationale: General meetings are meetings of the shareholders.

questions.question: Who are primarily responsible for taking the procedural steps necessary to establish a company and making the initial business preparations?
questions.answer: Promoters
questions.rationale: Promoters undertake incorporation and preliminary business activities.

questions.question: Under the Companies Act No. 07 of 2007, which document serves as the principal constitutional document of a company?
questions.answer: Articles of Association
questions.rationale: The Articles constitute the primary constitutional document.

questions.question: Which statement concerning debentures is legally correct?
options: A company may purchase or redeem its own debentures subject to applicable legal requirements.
A company is absolutely prohibited from acquiring its own debentures.
Debentures always confer voting rights identical to ordinary shares.
Debentures can only be issued by public companies.
questions.answer: A company may purchase or redeem its own debentures subject to applicable legal requirements.
questions.rationale: Companies may generally acquire their own debentures if statutory requirements are satisfied.

questions.question: Under the Companies Act No. 07 of 2007, who has primary responsibility for managing the affairs of a company?
options: The board of directors rather than the shareholders
The shareholders directly through day to day management
questions.answer: The board of directors rather than the shareholders
questions.rationale: Management powers are primarily vested in the board unless otherwise provided.

questions.question: Shares issued without any preferential or special rights attached are known as:
questions.answer: Ordinary shares
questions.rationale: Ordinary shares carry the standard rights of membership.

questions.question: Redeemable shares are best described as shares that:
options: May be bought back or redeemed by the company in accordance with their terms and the law.
Can never be cancelled after issue.
Automatically convert into debentures after one year.
Must always carry enhanced voting rights.
questions.answer: May be bought back or redeemed by the company in accordance with their terms and the law.
questions.rationale: Redeemable shares are capable of redemption subject to legal requirements.

questions.question: A company may generally make a call on shares when:
options: The call is made in accordance with the terms of issue and the company's constitution.
The company incurs an operating loss.
questions.answer: The call is made in accordance with the terms of issue and the company's constitution.
questions.rationale: Calls on shares must comply with governing legal and constitutional provisions.

questions.question: The primary basis for imposing liability upon experts whose reports or opinions appear in a company's prospectus is that:
options: Investors are entitled to rely upon expert statements that are materially false or misleading.
Experts automatically become company directors once their reports are published.
Experts guarantee the commercial success of the company.
Experts assume unlimited liability for every company debt.
questions.answer: Investors are entitled to rely upon expert statements that are materially false or misleading.
questions.rationale: Experts may incur liability where investors rely on inaccurate or misleading expert opinions included in a prospectus.
